newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower, pulled by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower, pulled by Wall Street.

text.p: French stocks fell on Thursday, pressured by a drop on Wall Street and weakness in the bonds and dollar, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 22.10 points, or 0.87 percent, at 2,508.18 at 0830 GMT, while the CAC-40 April futures contract was 19 points lower at 2,508.
Volume was 933 million francs in the first 20 minutes of trade.
Shares in Renault were down 2.4 percent at 128 francs after unions in France, Belgium and Spain called for labour stoppages on Friday to protest against the Vilvoorde plant closure.
One trader said the share was also pressured by a 43 percent drop in Renault's sales in Belgium, where it was one of the leaders, in March.

Lyonnaise des Eaux shares rose 1.86 percent to 548 francs. It reported net attributable profit last year of 1.35 billion francs, within market expectations. Lyonnaise said it aimed for a profit of more than 1.6 billion francs for 1997.
It also said its board unanimously favoured a merger with Cie de Suez. Suez has said its board also favours the move.
Alcatel Alsthom shares were down 3.98 percent at 651 francs. Market sources said Societe Generale was placing three million shares of Alcatel at 647 million francs per share.
Alcatel's bidding rival for Thomson-CSF, Lagardere , was up 0.56 percent at 179.10 francs.
"GEC's involvement in the bidding means that politicians in France will look more favourably on Lagardere's offer," a trader said.
Lagardere said on Wednesday that it was aware the British company was bidding for Thomson-CSF and that it did not regard the move as unfriendly.
